newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power steady despite oil, gas rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power steady despite oil, gas rally.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Northeast finished Monday mostly steady against Friday despite another rally in oil and natural gas prices on forecast of an Arctic blast in the eastern U.S. this week.
"With the weather somewhat mild, it won't affect us until next week," said a New York trader.
The region's temperatures would run 10 to 15 Fahrenheit degrees above normal through Wednesday, and turn colder by the weekend.
Swing natgas prices at the New York City gate rose 30 cents per million British thermal units (mmBtu) to the $4.60 area, reflecting soaring prices across the U.S.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, January Henry Hub gas futures settled up 61.6 cents at $4.467/mmBtu after posting an all-time record high of $4.560.
NYMEX January crude futures finished up $1.27 a barrel at $25.74 amid strength in heating oil prices.
Spot power prices in the New York Power Pool (NYPP) failed to get a boost from an unplanned shutdown of the 832 megawatt (MW) James A Fitzpatrick nuclear plant, market sources said.
The Scriba, N.Y., generating facility was manually shut Sunday during a weekend restart attempt for repairs of a leak in the electrical hydraulic control system.
In western NYPP, Tuesday electricity for peak, non-firm delivery was quoted $23.00-$24.00 and for off-peak, non-firm delivery near $15.00-$16.00, flat from Friday.
In eastern NYPP, Tuesday power for peak, non-firm delivery was again valued at $29.00-$30.00 and for off-peak, non-firm delivery $19.00-$20.00.
Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co today said the 910 MW Maine Yankee nuclear power plant could remain shut until the end of year because it discovered additional problem in an electrical cable system.

The plant was shut December 6 after engineers found a couple of cables to the plant's main control room had been improperly routed. Maine Yanke Atomic Power previously said it hoped to return the facility to production this week.

Despite news of an extended of the Maine Yankee, spot prices in the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL) finished flat to lower today on projection of lackluster demand for the next few days, market sources said.
Peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border was quoted near $34.00, down from Fridday's $35.00-$36.00 for Monday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Tuesday delivery to the NU border was remained in the $20.00-$21.00 area.
